sheets.title: North India 650 – 1200: Kannauj, Palas, Pratiharas, Rajputs
sheets.intro: Tripartite struggle, Palas, Pratiharas, Rajput kingdoms, Tarain.

keys.name: Tripartite struggle

rows.v: Palas (east) vs Gurjara-Pratiharas (centre-west) vs Rashtrakutas (Deccan)
Kannauj (Kanyakubja, Mahodaya) – Ganga trade, Harsha's old capital
Sakalottarapathanatha / Uttarapathaswami (lord of the north)
Vatsaraja (P) beat Dharmapala near Prayag; Dhruva (R) beat both – added Ganga, Yamuna to his emblem
Nagabhata II took Kannauj from Chakrayudha (Pala puppet); beat Dharmapala near Monghyr; Govinda III beat him, went home
Indrayudha, Vajrayudha, Chakrayudha – weak rulers of Kannauj
Pratiharas top by late 9th c.; all three drained → Rajput states → Turks

traps: Tripartite (Pala, Pratihara, Rashtrakuta) ≠ Tamil three crowned kings

keys.name: Palas of Bengal

rows.v: c. 750; elected to end matsyanyaya ("law of the fish"); Odantapuri (Bihar Sharif) – model for Tibet's Samye
c. 770 – 810; Kannauj darbar installing Chakrayudha (Khalimpur plate); Vikramashila; Somapura Mahavihara, Paharpur (UNESCO 1985); revived Nalanda; title Paramasaugata
c. 810 – 850; peak (Assam to Vindhyas); gave 5 villages to Balaputradeva's (Sailendra) Nalanda monastery
c. 988 – 1038; revived Palas; lost to Rajendra Chola (1022)
Beat the Kaivarta revolt (Divya) – Ramacharita of Sandhyakara Nandi
Vikramashila teacher; to Tibet 1040s
Black basalt, bronze icons; palm-leaf Prajnaparamita manuscripts
Called it "Ruhmi"; big army
Senas (Vijayasena), 12th c.

traps: Mahipala (Pala) lost to Rajendra Chola; Mahipala (Pratihara) lost Kannauj to Indra III

keys.name: Gurjara-Pratiharas

rows.v: "Doorkeeper" – from Lakshmana; origin Mandor (Jodhpur)
c. 730 – 760; Avanti (Ujjain); stopped the Arabs of Sind
c. 775 – 800; beat Dharmapala; lost to Dhruva
c. 800 – 833; Kannauj the capital; lost to Govinda III
c. 836 – 885; peak; Adivaraha, Prabhasa titles; Gwalior Prashasti
c. 885 – 910; poet Rajashekhara (Karpuramanjari, Kavyamimamsa, Balaramayana)
c. 912 – 944; al-Masudi came 915 – 16; lost Kannauj briefly to Indra III (916)
Fled Mahmud (1018); killed by Chandella Vidyadhara
Strongest foe of the Arabs, finest cavalry
Ranahastina

traps: Nagabhata I fought Arabs; Nagabhata II took Kannauj

rows.v: c. 831 – 845; founder, Pratihara feudatory
c. 925 – 950; Lakshmana temple (Vishnu), Khajuraho, 954
950 – 999; independent; Vishvanatha temple
1003 – 1035; resisted Mahmud; killed Rajyapala; Kandariya Mahadeva
1060 – 1100; Prabodhachandrodaya (Krishna Mishra)
1165 – 1203; Alha and Udal fell at Mahoba (1182) vs Prithviraj; Aibak took Kalinjar 1202 – 03
Khajuraho, Kalinjar, Mahoba
UNESCO 1986; 25 of 85 temples left; Hindu and Jain; Nagara
9th c.; founder; set up by Rashtrakutas
940 – 972; sacked Manyakheta 972 (Harsola plates show him a Rashtrakuta vassal)
972 – 995; poet; patron of Padmagupta, Dhanapala; killed by Tailapa II
1010 – 1055; Dhar; Bhoj Tal (Bhopal), Bhojshala, Bhojeshwar temple (Bhojpur); wrote Samarangana Sutradhara (architecture), Saraswati Kanthabharana, Rajamartanda; Kaviraja
Bhoja with Rajendra Chola and Kalachuris vs Western Chalukyas
Udaipur and Nagpur Prashastis
1305 – Alauddin's army killed Mahalakadeva

keys.name: Solankis (Chaulukyas) of Gujarat

rows.v: c. 940 – 995; Anhilwara (Patan)
1022 – 1064; Somnath sacked (1025); Modhera Sun temple (1026); minister Vimala built Vimal Vasahi, Dilwara (1031)
Stepwell by Queen Udayamati; UNESCO 2014; on the ₹100 note
1092 – 1142; took Malwa; Hemachandra (Siddha-Hema grammar); Rudra Mahalaya, Siddhpur
1143 – 1172; Jain under Hemachandra
Ghori's first defeat in India, by queen-mother Naikidevi's army
Aibak sacked Anhilwara 1197; Vaghelas; Luna Vasahi (1230, Vastupala – Tejapala); Karna Vaghela lost to Alauddin 1299
Maru-Gurjara

traps: Kayadara 1178 = Ghori’s first defeat; Tarain I 1191 = second

rows.v: Founded Dhillika (Delhi) – trad. 736, Anangpal I; Anangpal II built Lal Kot; Asigarh fort, Hansi
Founded Ajayameru (Ajmer) c. 1113
Anasagar lake; married Jayasimha Solanki's daughter
Took Delhi c. 1152; Harakeli Nataka; Sanskrit college at Ajmer (later Adhai Din ka Jhonpra)
Rai Pithora; c. 1177 – 1192; king at 11; Qila Rai Pithora
Prithviraja Vijaya (Jayanaka, Sanskrit, reliable); Prithviraj Raso (Chand Bardai, later, legend – Agnikula myth)

keys.name: Tarain and Chandawar

rows.v: 1191 – Prithviraj III beat Muhammad Ghori
1192 – Ghori beat and killed Prithviraj; Chauhan power fell
1194 – Ghori beat and killed Jaichandra Gahadavala
Taraori near Karnal, Haryana
Delhi Sultanate (Aibak, 1206)

Founder

Turushkadanda (linked to the Turks)
